question:
What fraction of the square is shaded?

[Figure 1](figures/1990_AMC_8_Q03_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The drawn diagonal suggests folding the square to compare its pieces without calculating their individual areas.

[Figure 1](figures/1990_AMC_8_Q03_question_fig1.svg)

Reflect across the diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner. The small shaded triangle matches the small unshaded triangle. The middle shaded piece matches the middle unshaded piece, and the top shaded piece matches the unshaded piece on the right.

Reflection preserves area, so each pair contains equal shaded and unshaded areas. Since the three pairs fill the square, half of the square is shaded. The fraction is \(\boxed{\tfrac12}\), choice \(\text{E}\).

nodes.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

nodes.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

nodes.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems. For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

nodes.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

nodes.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

edges.reason: Division introduces equal sharing, a useful conceptual bridge. Folding one whole into equal paper parts establishes a unit fraction without division notation or the inverse-multiplication interpretation.
The target explicitly distinguishes boundary length from area. Perimeter meaning is required for that contrast, not all rectangle/square perimeter computations.
Line and ray experience helps describe an axis of reflection. Folding a paper shape to make its halves coincide can identify symmetry without classifying line/ray/segment first.
edges.scope: describing the axis of symmetry as a line
